observations.detail: The ending places the bookmark inside Nisa's reading book, which lacks a canonical object identity in the closed initial entity set. The extractor leaves container null/inventory-held and reports uncertainty rather than representing that explicit terminal containment.

Final reviewer claims the prose never clearly removes the bookmark from the atlas, but writer-2 explicitly says Nisa removes it into her palm and returns the atlas to the shelf. A protruding bookmark tip does not inherently make containment paradoxical.

Final review R0343 cites an earlier uncertainty dialogue instead of the criticised memory passage; R0535 cites the notebook search instead of the bookmark recovery. Hash/range binding proves which text was cited, not that it supports the claim.

Final review treats the book-pile memory detail as unsupported, although first review suggested leaving the atlas on the table or book stack. This should be evaluated as guard/repair contract drift, not assumed writer incapacity.
